Header: Thaumatotibia leucotreta (syn. Chryptophlebia leucotreta ) False codling moth in English

Prevention: Avoid intercropping or growing cotton, tomato, okra, eggplant
pepper or sweet potato near the orchard because they are alternative hosts to false codling moth pest
Monitoring: Check every fifth tree in an orchard
Check trees at flowering and fruit set for 1 cm big brown moths with a dark coppery brown band at the tip of the wings
Look for the moths early in the morning as they are inactive during the day
Control the insect when you see at least 10-20 moths on 30% of the trees inspected
Use pheromone traps for effective long-term monitoring.
Check the traps once weekly during the fruiting period.
Control pest at 60-80 moth catches per trap per week
Look for 1 mm diameter holes/ burrows and frass on the rind of the fruit.
This is the larvae entry hole
Look for 1 to 1 ½ cm long light pink larvae with a dark brown head inside the fruit
Look for above signs especially during early fruit development and entire fruiting stage
When larvae have entered the fruits, action is too late this season, but may warrant action next season
Direct Control: Heavily irrigate an infested field to kill the pupa in the soil
Dudutech company outlets) several times while the fruits are susceptible to the pest.
Up to about 125,000 are per hectare.
Pick all infested fruits (both on trees and those fallen on the ground) and destroy by burying at least 50cm deep twice every week during fruiting stage.
EC at the rate of 20 - 25ml/20l of water to reduce infestation
